legacy_import_rules: Archive signed Java potential[5], full socket[3], computed/original socketState, source encoder variant/config/addon provenance and any received raw bytes independently. Five native options plus one flags word cannot losslessly hold both namespaces.
Java remainder is signed: default socket=-1 emits0xFFFF, never zero; native current Go zero-potential golden retains option4/5/flags=FFFF. Do not silently normalize historical blank bytes.
Example socket1=3061001 and3062001 both project1001: no inverse. socket3 remainder can set native option-visibility bits accidentally; this is evidence of mismatch, not semantic conversion.
Do not infer DB p4/p5 from wire option4/5 under six-short Java path; those came from sockets. Do not infer full socket IDs from remainders.

For new native equipment a separate versioned model can hold five valid option IDs and opaque flags; derive raw state from explicit sealed/revealed tier, never concatenate Java socket projection. This is a new codec, not lossless Java-import conversion.

magnify.required: hidden state1; current USE magnifier/positive bag equipment; Java network path casts slots to signed byte and has worn fallback commented. Native accepts I16/worn, so negative/wide slots require a deliberate validated adapter, not Java cast emulation.
magnify.lines: 2+(p2!=0)+(p3!=0)+(p4!=0); p5 is not counted; 2..5 random draws, but i3/i4 set p4/p5=0, so only p1..3 are retained even if extra draws consumed
magnify.candidate: uniform random choice among all potentialCache option rows, then reject until fixed info floor(reqLevel/10)<=selected item floor(reqLevel/10), optionTypeFits, potentialIDFits. WZ weights not read. Duplicate IDs allowed across lines. HashMap iteration affects deterministic seed mapping but not uniform row probabilities.
magnify.band: Java candidate row index=floor(itemReq/10), clamp>=20 to19 only if mystery=true (annotation defaulttrue). Native and Java PlayerStats ordinary value index=max(0,(itemReq-1)/10). Maintain generation membership threshold separately from stat value band; replacing threshold with native index changes eligible set at exact tens.
magnify.membership_example: itemReq10 weapon can choose10221 with optionReq10 because1<=1; rejecting it using native index0 is not faithful. Band row selection itself does not change membership while fresh immutable opID/info are identical across bands.
magnify.later_lines: same tier orone below, intersect10000..59999; IDs50000..59999 therefore pass global bound but are unreachable for valid tier17..20, as are1..9999 and60000+
magnify.special: if accepted40650/40656, nextInt100>Q mutates shared StructItemOption.opID=10001; annotation Q10 means retain11%, replace89% on first accepted special draw, not10%/90%. No revalidation after replacement. On firstline a downgraded10001 can force reroll of all lines until equipment state reaches requested tier.
magnify.shared_mutation: mutation is only selected band of one original cache row; future draws of that row use opID10001 while original info/type/data/mapkey remain special. It persists until Java process cache reload, affects other characters and is not immutable-catalog semantics. Subsequent rare acceptance can give duplicate10001 rows and skew candidate weighting. Do not claim immutable local substitution reproduces this process-history behavior.
magnify.loop: If no compatible candidates, Java loops without bound; if index>=20 and mystery=false, indexed get may throw after fee was charged. Go must preflight viable pool and atomic resource settlement rather than reproduce hangs/partial debit.
magnify.outcome: Java charges meso before random loop and removes tool after success; eventual transactional Go should conserve both and replay same result. Success F2 is cosmetic, inventory equipment update is authority.
magnify.tool_level_boundary_difference: Java floor(itemReq/10)<=3/7/12 allows itemReq<=39/79/129 for2460000/1/2, whereas original native UI tests raw itemReq<=30/70/120 (prior63-primary contract).2460003 bypasses bound. Preserve this difference explicitly; do not claim original UI will submit every Java-accepted target.

minimum_model_proposal.equipment: Versioned PotentialMetadata{tier17..20, revealed bool, lineCount2..5, options[5]uint16, nativeFlagsuint16, policyVersion}; sealed tier andlineCount are server data distinct from raw native state. minimum_model_proposal.catalog: Parent owns immutable206-row/20-band WZ catalog with all original fields/weights/hash retained. Preserve weights as metadata without using them for Java-compatible selection.
minimum_model_proposal.policy: Pure versioned eligibility/rank/line/fee/result functions plus injected bounded RNG; candidates validated before spending; record config anddraw/result under one atomic item/tool/meso receipt. Stat lookup uses native/Java PlayerStats ordinary band; unsupported special item overrides need explicit support orfail closed.

Native five-field codec is still required even when first vertical generates3 only. Safe atomic settlement andmetadata preservation first; do not advertise cube/socket/five-line generation orall option stat behaviors.
minimum_model_proposal.known_non_equivalence: New coherent native codec fixes Java socket projection; immutable special replacement fixes Java cache mutation; blocking broken epic state0/1 avoidsinvalid-tier behavior. These are explicit compatibility divergences, not facts about legacy intent. Full strict-compat requires a separately modeled shared effective-ID overlay andlegacy edge transitions.
minimum_model_proposal.if_scope_changes_need_explicit_policy: Do not invent WZ success rates/weighted roll/guaranteed-epic semantics. If desired they change observed Java balancing and need an explicit requirement; no such requirement is inferred. Whether to preserve process-global cache corruption versus versioned immutable corrected policy is a compatibility choice to agree with root before enabling special rolls, not a reason to block schema/catalog work.
